classification.difficultyReason: Use supplied partial fractions to solve the initial-value problem, evaluate the population and apply exponential decay to identify the explicitly requested carrying-capacity limit.

content.prompt:
A seal colony satisfies $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=\dfrac14P\left(1-\dfrac{P}{800}\right)$, $P(0)=100$, $t$ in years.

Use
$$\frac{800}{P(800-P)}=\frac1P+\frac1{800-P}.$$
Find $P(t)$, $P(8)$, and show that the long-term population is the carrying capacity. Give $P(8)$ to the nearest whole seal.

answer.short: $P(t)=\dfrac{800}{1+7e^{-t/4}}$; $P(8)\approx411$ seals. As $t\to\infty$, $P(t)\to800$ seals, the carrying capacity.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{dt}{dP}&=\frac{3200}{P(800-P)}\\
\frac{dt}{dP}&=4\left(\frac1P+\frac1{800-P}\right)\\
t&=4\bigl(\ln|P|-\ln|800-P|\bigr)+D\\
\ln\left|\frac{P}{800-P}\right|&=\frac t4-\frac D4\\
\frac{P}{800-P}&=Ae^{t/4}.
\end{aligned}$$
Using $P(0)=100$,
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{100}{700}&=Ae^0\\
A&=\frac17.
\end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{P}{800-P}&=\frac17e^{t/4}\\
7P&=(800-P)e^{t/4}\\
P(7+e^{t/4})&=800e^{t/4}\\
P(t)&=\frac{800}{1+7e^{-t/4}}\\
P(8)&=\frac{800}{1+7e^{-2}}\\
P(8)&\approx411.
\end{aligned}$$
After 8 years, the population is approximately 411 seals. As $t\to\infty$, $e^{-t/4}\to0$, so $P(t)\to800$ seals, the carrying capacity.
